Estimate abundance and density from removal samples

Source: R/abundance.R
abundance.Rd

Abundance is estimated as \(\hat N = T / P\), where \(T\) is the total catch over the passes of a sample and \(P\) is the cumulative capture probability, see capture_prob.

Usage

abundance(object, newdata = NULL, area = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

an efp2 fitted model

newdata

an optional data.frame as for capture_prob, which must also contain the counts used as the response in the model

area

an optional name of a column in the data giving the area fished, or a vector of areas with one value per row of the data. If given, density (abundance per unit area) is also returned.

level

the confidence level

Value

a data.frame with one row per sample, in the order the samples first appear in the data, with columns id, catch the total catch, P, N the estimated abundance, its standard error se, and confidence limits lower and upper. If area is given there are also columns area, density, density_lower and density_upper.

Details

The variance of \(\hat N\) combines the binomial sampling variation in the catch, given \(P\), and the uncertainty in the estimate of \(P\) (Huggins, 1989): $$\textrm{var}(\hat N) \approx \hat N (1 - P) / P + \hat N^2 (1 - P)^2 \textrm{var}(\textrm{logit}(P)).$$ Confidence intervals are computed on the log scale, and the lower limit is not less than the total catch. When the total catch is zero the estimated abundance is zero and the confidence limits are NA.

References

Huggins, R. M. (1989) On the statistical analysis of capture experiments. Biometrika, 76, 133-140. doi:10.1093/biomet/76.1.133

See also

capture_prob

Examples

ef2_data$pass12 <- factor(pmin(ef2_data$pass, 2))
ef2_data$sampleID <- as.numeric(factor(paste(ef2_data$date,
  ef2_data$siteID, ef2_data$lifestage)))
ef2_data <- ef2_data[order(ef2_data$sampleID, ef2_data$pass), ]
m1 <- efp2(count ~ lifestage + pass12, data = ef2_data,
  pass = pass, id = sampleID)
head(abundance(m1, area = "area"))
